messages.subject: visualisation_sleep.pdf
parts:
We analyze a larger data set of approx. 50 data records over 21 days or 30 days. We would like to analyze all files at once in GGIR. Our data records are named with a 4 to 6 digit ID. The data was recorded with GENEActiv, the analysis with GGIR 3.1-5 and R 4.4.2, so everything is completely up-to-date.
The file visualization_sleep.pdf is output as usual with all nights, whereby one line per night is displayed as a diagram.

Problem: The ID is at the beginning of the line. However, this is cut off by the first 2 to 4 characters, which is why some of the individual diagrams cannot be assigned. Is this problem known? Is there a solution?
If I only evaluate a .bin source file, less is cut off, but as soon as the night goes from 9 to 10, one more character is cut off (because night9 is 1 character shorter than night10....).

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] visualisation_sleep.pdf
parts:
Hi Maximilian,

I am aware of this limitation of the visualreport, which has existed for many years. One way to address it is by using shorter IDs, which may require that you rename your accelerometer files or that you change the way in which GGIR extracts the participant ID with parameter idloc. If you could share an example participant ID, corresponding accelerometer filename and your current idloc parameter value then I am happy to have a quick look at it.

The alternative route is to revise how GGIR creates the visualisation and adds the ID to it. For example, we could write the ID in between the lines and show only the night number in the margin. I am happy to do that as a (small) paid consultancy project. Please send me direct message if you are interested. If you or someone else wants to do this work and make a code pull request which I can then merge that is also fine with me.

Best regards,
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] visualisation_sleep.pdf
parts:
Hello Vincent,
thank you very much for your reply and also for the offer of special customization.
I have now noticed when checking the idloc source that the ID here contained many spaces at the end.

For other users to understand: We use GENEActiv, these trackers are read out with “GENEAchtiv PC Software” --> the .bin file is created. When examining the .bin file in the editor, I noticed that line 39 begins with “Subject Code:”, followed by the ID, e.g. “1234”. The line is always padded with spaces so that the ID is 20 characters long. This means that line 39:
“Subject Code:1234                    ”

The solution is therefore simple: delete the spaces in all .bin files or read the ID from the file name (idloc = 2   --> https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#idloc )

Thank you Vincent for your support

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] visualisation_sleep.pdf
parts:
I would not do that.

If there would be any indication that all GENEActiv users have this issue then it would be really bad to recommend everyone to edit their file names as it risks accidentally removing parts from the real participant ID. I only recommended editing the filenames because I thought this was something specific to your dataset and that you were using idloc = 2 with filenames that look like "123       _15238.bin".

I do not understand why you are referring to the ID stored inside the file, because GGIR either extracts the ID from there (idloc = 1) which is not affected by the filename or GGIR extracts the ID from the filename which does not care about the ID stored inside the file.

I have never seen spaces in GENEActiv filenames, and with parameter idloc = 2 we can extract the ID from the filename without problems.

As I suggested in my previous message I can only really help if you share R code, example filenames, and/or example data.

Thanks,

Vincent

messages.author: 94ceb93e0c5036f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] visualisation_sleep.pdf
parts:
Thanks for the quick reply!

To set the record straight: so far we have not used idloc --> so idloc = 1 (default), which means that GGIR takes the ID from the .bin file. Here I assume that the ID is extracted from line 39 “Subject Code:”. However, there are spaces in this line as already described.
The file name is of course without spaces.

Unfortunately, I cannot provide any of our patient data records for data protection reasons. However, I have created a short recording.
The file name (automatically defined by the GENEActiv software) is “12345_left wrist_071023_2024-11-28 12-33-45.bin”.
Line 39 in the file is “Subject Code:12345               ”.

The extraction of the ID from the file name before “_” ( idlock = 2) works well for us - I tried this yesterday in the data set with approx. 50 21-day recordings.

However, if I want to use idloc = 1 for our data sets (and I assume that this is the case for all GENEActiv data sets) and want to avoid the IDs being cutt off in visualization_sleep.pdf, then you would either have to open each .bin file and remove all spaces after the ID in “Subject Code” (line 39), or you would have to teach ID loc to ignore spaces after the ID.


This is our used code:

library(GGIR)
 
GGIR(                   # Erklärungen siehe https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html

  #  To Do! ####
  maxdur = 21,                       
  datadir = "C:/GENEActiv/data/Test/"
  outputdir = "C:/GENEActiv/results",
 
  # 3.2. GGIR Standardskript ####  
  print.filename = TRUE,        # Dateiname wird im Ausgabefelt von R ausgegeben (zur Information zum Fortschitt)
  mode = c(1,2,3,4,5),          # gibt an, welcher der GGIR Parts (1 bis 6) ausgeführt werden soll
  overwrite = TRUE,             # Ob vorherige Ausgaben im Outputordner überschreiben (TRUE)  
  do.report = c(2,4,5),         # Reportdateien, die erstellt werden sollen (möglich von Part 2, 4 und 5)
  idloc =2,                     # definiert Quelle der ID (1 --> aus .BIN-Datei - Problem mit Leerzeichen bei visual_sleep.pdf, 2 --> alles vor "_" --> https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#idloc)
 
  # 3.3. GGIR Part 2 ####
  # === Basisanalyse (non-wear detection, basic descriptive summary of accelerations)
strategy = 1,
hrs.del.start = 0,
hrs.del.end = 0,
includedaycrit = 16,
includenightcrit = 16,
qwindow = c(0,24),
mvpathreshold = c(100),       # MVPA = Moderate or Vigorous activity; Beschleunigungsschwelle für die MVPA-Schätzung [in mg?]; bei Angabe mehrerer Werte (,), werden mehrere MVPA Werte errechnet
bout.metric = 4,
excludefirstlast = FALSE,

 
  # 3.4. GGIR Part 3 + 4 ####
  # === für Schlafanalyse
def.noc.sleep = 1,          
outliers.only = FALSE,
criterror = 4,
do.visual = TRUE,

  # 3.5. GGIR Part 5 ####
  # === für Analyse der physical activity und Reporterstellung
threshold.lig = c(30),        # Nummerischer Schwellenwert für leichte körperliche Aktivität (in Abgrenzung zu Inaktivität). Bei Angabe mehrerer Werte =c(30,40), dann erfolgt die Analyse für die einzelnen Schwellwerte separat; Bezieht sich auf ENMO [mg]
threshold.mod = c(100),       # Siehe „threshold.lig“; grenzt leichte von moderater Aktivität ab
threshold.vig = c(400),       # Siehe „threshold.lig“; grenzt moderate vom schwerer Aktivität ab
boutcriter = 0.8,             # Bezüglich „mvpathreshold“ (in Part2): Anteil des Zeitabschnitts, welcher über der bei „mvpathreshold“ angegebenen Schwelle liegen muss
boutcriter.in = 0.9,          # Gibt den Anteil des Zeitabschnitts an, welcher unter der Schwelle „threshold.lig“ liegen muss, damit das zur Inaktivität gezählt werden kann
boutcriter.lig = 0.8,         # Siehe „boutcriter.in“; Anteil des Bout (Zeitabschnitts) zwischen den Grenzen t…lig und t…mod
boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,        # Siehe „boutcriter.in“ Boutanteil, der oberhalb des Grenzwerts threshold.mod liegen muss
boutdur.in = c(10,20,30),     # ???? https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#boutdur-in
boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10),      #
boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),     #

  # 3.6. GGIR Report ####
timewindow = c("WW"),
viewingwindow = 1,
visualreport = TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] visualisation_sleep.pdf
parts:
If your file names are in the format "12345_left wrist_071023_2024-11-28 12-33-45.bin" then using idloc = 2 should work fine without the need to modify .bin files. This will extract the character string 12345 from the file name as the characters that are before the first underscore in the file name.

Could you please explain why this does not work for you?

If you cannot provide me with a clear motivation I plan to deprecate idloc = 1 functionality next year as I see that it could have really damaging side-effects if more research groups started to fiddle with their .bin files.

Best,

Vincent

parts:
I think there is a misunderstanding here.

The function idloc = 2 works very well for us. We can also continue to work well with it.

I opened this thread when we were not yet working with idloc = 2, but were using idloc = 1.

In our case, idloc = 1 worked really well despite the blank character problem, if you only evaluate one data set. This is because you know which data set it is and it is not a problem if the label is partially cut off.

We have only been evaluating several data sets at once for a short time and we have encountered the problem that the ID is cut off in the graphical display visualization_sleep.pdf (idloc =1).

Since, as I said, we are now getting on very well with IDloc = 2, we no longer have any problems.
However, since I assume that all users and also future users who work with GENEActiv and have to familiarize themselves with the functionality of GGIR could encounter the problem if they have set idloc = 1, the following (or similar) implementation for the variable idloc = 1 would be desirable:

id_clean <- sub(“\\s+$”, “”, id) # disregard all spaces at the end of the ID

Vincent van Hees schrieb am Sonntag, 8. Dezember 2024 um 15:30:14 UTC+1:
If your file names are in the format "12345_left wrist_071023_2024-11-28 12-33-45.bin" then using idloc = 2 should work fine without the need to modify .bin files. This will extract the character string 12345 from the file name as the characters that are before the first underscore in the file name.

Could you please explain why this does not work for you?

If you cannot provide me with a clear motivation I plan to deprecate idloc = 1 functionality next year as I see that it could have really damaging side-effects if more research groups started to fiddle with their .bin files.

Best,

Vincent

Vincent van Hees schrieb am Donnerstag, 28. November 2024 um 14:54:54 UTC+1:
I would not do that.

If there would be any indication that all GENEActiv users have this issue then it would be really bad to recommend everyone to edit their file names as it risks accidentally removing parts from the real participant ID. I only recommended editing the filenames because I thought this was something specific to your dataset and that you were using idloc = 2 with filenames that look like "123 _15238.bin".

I do not understand why you are referring to the ID stored inside the file, because GGIR either extracts the ID from there (idloc = 1) which is not affected by the filename or GGIR extracts the ID from the filename which does not care about the ID stored inside the file.

I have never seen spaces in GENEActiv filenames, and with parameter idloc = 2 we can extract the ID from the filename without problems.

As I suggested in my previous message I can only really help if you share R code, example filenames, and/or example data.

Thanks,

Vincent

Hello Vincent,
thank you very much for your reply and also for the offer of special customization.
I have now noticed when checking the idloc source that the ID here contained many spaces at the end.

For other users to understand: We use GENEActiv, these trackers are read out with “GENEAchtiv PC Software” --> the .bin file is created. When examining the .bin file in the editor, I noticed that line 39 begins with “Subject Code:”, followed by the ID, e.g. “1234”. The line is always padded with spaces so that the ID is 20 characters long. This means that line 39:
“Subject Code:1234 ”

The solution is therefore simple: delete the spaces in all .bin files or read the ID from the file name (idloc = 2 --> https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#idloc )

Thank you Vincent for your support
